page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server includes a 77 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC 7763 processor demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2701.89. However, its multi-core performance in the same test is weak, scoring in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the passmark memory score and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks both fall into the bottom 10%, with read-only small block bandwidth measured at 127.65 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, but multi-threaded workloads, such as software compilation with Clang and ray tracing, score in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ads_v5 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated AMD EPYC resources, but users face significant performance tradeoffs. The limited 2 vCPU capacity and weak multi-core scaling restrict its utility for parallel processing. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks both rank in the bottom 10%, indicating that this instance is poorly suited for high-throughput database hosting or intensive caching layers. Static web serving throughput is also low at 2.55 GB/sec. Consequently, this server is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, or development environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or parallelized compute power.
